newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures post hefty rise as yen falls.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures post hefty rise as yen falls.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures sustained early gains to end sharply up on Wednesday as the yen's weakness and a surge in technology stocks on Wall Street spurred buying of export-oriented issues on the underlying cash market.
After a firm start, Nikkei 225 September futures continued to gain ground, ending 390 points higher at 20,435.
Market turnover was well above levels seen in recent days at 20,345 lots.
Dealers said the market also received a boost from Tuesday's announcement that the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd and Swiss Bank Corp would form a strategic alliance.
"The market took that as very good news. Most of the banking stocks went up," a trader at a Japanese brokerage said.

Reports of North and South Korean soldiers exchanging fire at the border briefly dampened sentiment, but players were quick to dismiss the potential significance of the news and cover their positions, he said.
The September Nikkei's close above the 20,300-20,400 resistance band boded well for the near-term, but the contract would need to negotiate a barrier at 20,600 to head higher, chartists said.
On Taiwan futures, the July contract ended down 1.0 at 406.3 on volume of 1,774 lots.
Dealers said the contract's persistent discount to the MSCI cash index suggested an underlying bearish view of the market.
